problem: The applicability condition requires only that nltl:tankType exists, but never restricts its value to the two required tank categories; instead it tests unrelated rdf:type assertions. A tank with an arbitrary tankType value can therefore be treated as applicable, while a required tank lacking that extra property can be skipped.
required_change: Encode the tank-type applicability directly through the canonical nltl:tankType representation, explicitly limiting it to oil residue tanks and oily bilge water holding tanks, and remove the unconstrained existence check and unrelated substitute classification. Locked resolution: use exactly https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#tankType.
regression_guard: Preserve both specified tank categories and do not broaden applicability to unrelated components.

problem: The mandatory nltl:individualTankCapacity and quantity-value triples are required for the SPARQL solution to exist, so a relevant tank with missing capacity is silently ignored rather than producing a conformance failure or an explicit incomplete-input result.
required_change: Ensure each applicable tank cannot bypass validation when its individual capacity is absent or unusable; enforce the required capacity input before evaluating the >30 m3 exception.
regression_guard: Preserve per-individual-tank evaluation and the >30 m3 exception without allowing missing capacity to evade the rule.
